turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: (laughs) Ah, I think you're getting a little mixed up with the actual McGurk effect. The McGurk effect actually involves visual and auditory cues that influence how we perceive speech sounds, not seeing pictures of strawberries. In the classic experiment, people are shown a video of someone saying a syllable, but the audio is manipulated to say something else. That's what leads to the fascinating phenomenon where our brains combine the visual and auditory cues to create a new sound.
